If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to offset pessimism.  
For mid-horizon (8–15 days), if sentiment swings from positive to negative, shift forecast downward by 0.5–1.0% per sentiment reversal.  
For late-horizon (16–30 days), if sentiment remains neutral (0.33–0.67) and forecast is above true, reduce by 0.5–1.0% to align with mean reversion.  
If sentiment is positive but forecast is consistently above true, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for all horizons to correct for sentiment-driven overconfidence.  
If sentiment is negative but forecast is consistently below true, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for all horizons to correct for sentiment-driven underestimation.
